summary.intent: Review all 7 project docs in .planning/codebase/ for stale content accumulated since their March 2026 generation, and update them against the live codebase. Then push the changes as a focused PR.
summary.outcome: A multi-agent audit-verify-apply workflow fixed 87 confirmed drift items across all 7 docs. The user then decided to remove internal package/crate version columns from STACK.md entirely (they churn too fast), obsoleting ~13 of the workflow's own fixes. Changes were committed on a fresh branch off origin/main; the session ended mid-PR-creation.

repo: Internal package/crate versions in planning docs are too volatile to maintain; .release-please-manifest.json is the authoritative source and should be referenced instead of inlining versions.
Rust toolchain pin is channel=1.88 (not 1.93+), lives at apps/desktop/src-tauri/rust-toolchain.toml — there is no root-level rust-toolchain.toml.
multiformats ^13.4.2 is a direct TEE worker dependency again (not replaced by @cipherbox/core as a stale doc claimed).
commit-msg git hook is now an Entire CLI wrapper — commitlint is no longer run locally and is enforced via PR-title CI only.
Staging deploy tags format: staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N (not staging-v<version>-rc-N).
e2e.yml was split into ci-e2e.yml (dispatcher) → web-e2e.yml / desktop-e2e.yml; build-desktop.yml became desktop-staging-release.yml triggered by cipherbox-desktop-v* tags.
axios is pinned exactly at 1.13.2 (no caret) in both web and api-client.
Prettier config now lives in prettier.config.js (es5 trailing commas, 100-char width).
TEE worker IPNS republish interval is 6h (was 3h in docs).
FUSE mkdir-retry concern in CONCERNS.md was resolved with a landed PR and regression test.

code.finding: multiformats ^13.4.2 is a direct dependency — it was incorrectly removed from the stack doc as 'replaced by @cipherbox/core'
Imports CID from multiformats/cid, confirming it is still a live direct dependency
channel = "1.88" — this is the sole Rust toolchain pin; no root-level rust-toolchain.toml exists

workflow: Three-phase multi-agent doc review (audit → adversarial verify → apply) with conservative bias is effective for catching drift without introducing bad edits.
Adversarial verification before applying is critical — it prevented incorrect changes from landing.
Running prettier after doc edits as a final hygiene step is important to avoid formatting noise in diffs.
When a current branch has already been squash-merged, branch fresh off origin/main rather than reusing the stale local branch.
1Password commit signing requires running git commit outside the sandbox with a timeout guard.

Workflow applied ~13 version-column fixes that were immediately made obsolete by the user's follow-up decision — front-loading a design conversation about doc structure could save wasted agent cycles.

friction: The workflow cited a root-level rust-toolchain.toml that does not exist; required a separate manual verification step to find the actual pin location.

~13 of the workflow's 23 STACK.md fixes (all per-package/crate version bumps) were immediately obsoleted when the user decided to remove version columns — the design question should have been asked before the workflow ran.
1Password signer adds commit latency and requires unsandboxed bash execution with a timeout guard, complicating the commit step.
Current local branch (v1.1 closeout work) had already been squash-merged via PR #524 but was not on remote, creating an ambiguous state that required investigation before branching.
open_items: PR creation was in progress at end of session — not confirmed as successfully opened.
External dependency versions in STACK.md are still inlined; user was offered the option to strip those too but did not decide.
CONCERNS.md keeps resolved items under '(RESOLVED)' headings for historical context — user was asked whether to strip them entirely but did not decide.
undici ^7.24.6 was added to TEE-specific deps in STACK.md as an SSRF-hardened HTTP agent — worth verifying this is correctly documented alongside the multiformats restoration.
